contentBlocks.body: A dict maps keys to values, like a JavaScript object or Map. Keys are written in quotes and accessed with brackets; there is no dot access. Reading a missing key with d[key] raises a KeyError instead of returning undefined, so use d.get(key, default) when a key may be absent. Dicts keep insertion order.

contentBlocks.code:
user = {"name": "Ada", "age": 36}
print(user["name"])            # Ada
print(user.get("email", "-"))  # -   (no KeyError)
user["email"] = "ada@x.dev"    # add or update
print("age" in user)           # True  (checks keys)
for key, value in user.items():
    print(key, value)

contentBlocks.body: A set is an unordered collection of unique values, like a JavaScript Set, but with math operators built in: | is union, & is intersection, and - is difference. Membership tests with `in` are fast on sets and dicts.
Dict keys must be hashable (immutable): strings, numbers and tuples work, lists do not. A tuple like (row, col) makes a handy key for grid coordinates.

knowledgeItems.prompt: What happens with user = {"name": "Ada"} and print(user["email"])?

payload.explanation: Bracket access requires the key to exist. user.get("email") would return None instead.
Empty braces create an empty dict. Use set() for an empty set.
& is set intersection: the values present in both sets.
